# Code of Conduct

We want contributors and users to be able to ask questions, report problems and disagree about technical decisions without harassment. These expectations apply to repository issues, pull requests, reviews and other project spaces.

## Expected behavior

- Treat participants respectfully, regardless of identity, experience or background.
- Discuss code, evidence and user needs rather than attacking a person.
- Give actionable feedback and acknowledge mistakes or corrections.
- Respect privacy. Do not post another person's private information or confidential source material.
- Keep discussion relevant and avoid spam, threats, sexual harassment or discriminatory language.

## Reporting and moderation

Report concerns to the repository maintainers using a private contact method they publish on their GitHub profiles. If none is available, ask for a private channel in a minimal issue without naming affected people or posting sensitive details. Use GitHub's abuse-reporting tools for immediate platform-level concerns.

Maintainers may edit or remove harmful content, restrict participation or close discussions to protect the community. They should consider context, explain moderation decisions when appropriate and handle private reports discreetly. This policy does not promise a response time or override GitHub's own terms.

Contributors may communicate in Chinese or English. Good-faith questions and respectful technical disagreement are welcome.
